paragraphs: Our Language Week, posted by May. I love English, so I write about our language lessons. I also write the emails to our pen pals, so English is important to me. We study two languages at school, Thai and English. Every pupil in our class has the same weekly timetable. Here are our language lessons. The timetable is next to the door, and we read it every day.

Monday: Thai at nine o'clock. Tuesday: English at nine o'clock. Wednesday: spelling practice at ten o'clock. Thursday: English at nine o'clock, and the club after lunch. Friday: the weekly quiz at ten o'clock. Each lesson is one hour long. We have a short break after each lesson.

Teacher Kim gives us homework two times a week. On Tuesday, we write five sentences about our day. On Wednesday, we practice ten new words, and we spell them. Mia writes new words in a small notebook. She puts a little picture next to each word. "Is ten words enough?" asked Mia. "It is enough for me," said Leo. "I need more practice," said Mia. "Then read a story every night," said Teacher Kim. "New words are easy to learn in a story."

The Friday quiz is short, so nobody is afraid of it. Teacher Kim gives each pupil a pen and a sheet of paper. Then she says ten words, and we write them. The room is quiet, and everybody thinks hard. At the end, we write one sentence with one of the words. Last Friday, Leo wrote "libary" for "library". Luckily, it was only one mistake. He laughed and said, "Now I will never forget it."

After the quiz, we relax and listen to a story. Teacher Kim reads for twenty minutes, and the room is quiet. Last Friday, Mia had ten out of ten, so we celebrated. We clapped, and Mia smiled. Everybody feels happy on Friday afternoon. It is a good way to start the weekend. We go home with a smile. I think that a language week is a happy week. Which language lesson do you like best?
